claims.text: The multiscale model will predict conductivity more accurately than conventional perfect-crystal analytical predictions in both the 0–200 K and 300–1200 K regimes.
Bulk HfNbTaTiZr is single phase in the proposed initial state.
The proposed HfNbTaTiZr specimen has a BCC lattice structure.
The proposed specimen contains a controlled oxygen concentration of 1 wt.%.
A 1 wt.% oxygen concentration occurs in experimentally measured HfNbTaTiZr specimens.
Defects significantly affect transport in HfNbTaTiZr at 0–200 K.
Thermal excitations are important to transport in HfNbTaTiZr at 300–1200 K.
Defect evolution is important to transport in HfNbTaTiZr at 300–1200 K.
Point defects introduce additional carrier or phonon scattering centers.
Oxygen impurities introduce additional carrier or phonon scattering centers.
Perfect-crystal models omit the additional scattering caused by point defects and oxygen impurities.
Defect scattering dominates the reduction in conductivity at low temperatures.
Oxygen-related scattering is especially important to the low-temperature reduction in conductivity.
Anharmonicity significantly affects transport at higher temperatures.
Defect interactions significantly affect transport at higher temperatures.
Modeling defect, oxygen, anharmonic, and defect-interaction effects will bring simulated transport properties closer to measurements.
The integrated model will reduce prediction error by at least 30% relative to conventional perfect-crystal predictions.
The integrated model will reproduce both the temperature-dependent trends and absolute conductivity values in both specified temperature regimes.
Conventional defect-free analytical models typically overestimate conductivity because they neglect defect- and oxygen-induced scattering.
The proposed model is applicable to bulk HfNbTaTiZr containing up to approximately 1 wt.% oxygen in the 0–200 K and 300–1200 K ranges, but may be unreliable at higher oxygen contents or above 1200 K.
